summary: The inner of Port Dalhousie's two range lights: an octagonal wooden tower built in 1898 after lightning burned its predecessor, dark since 1988.

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett directory).

events.note: Funds for nails and wicking for a Port Dalhousie lighthouse
Severe gale destroyed the earlier lighthouse and injured most of the east pier
Circular wooden lighthouse, about 13 m (44 ft), capped the east pier
Lamp exploded; fire badly damaged the lighting apparatus and lantern room
Square wooden front range tower on a new pier about 300 ft north
Foundation found settling; new tower built, old lantern reused, $2,157.51
Struck by lightning at 8:05 a.m., 12 August 1898, and burned to the ground
Present octagonal wooden rear tower built on shore east of the pier, $2,943.19; construction from October 1898 (Rowlett gives 1899)

Ownership transferred to the City of St. Catharines
Restored by the Friends of the Port Dalhousie Lighthouse, 2000 to 2002

corrections.why: The record's agency is cut off; the City's own heritage page and the Rowlett directory name the City of St. Catharines as owner.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives 1898 (Wikidata) and Rowlett gives 1899. The City says construction of the present tower began in October 1898, and the story uses 1898. The 1852 first year is the station's establishment; the present tower is the 1898 replacement.

The record's 1852 first year is the station establishment date (Rowlett). LighthouseFriends describes a circular wooden lighthouse on the east pier in 1850, which the 1898 tower replaced, so the two dates describe different towers.

LighthouseFriends' map line puts the light at the inner end of the east pier; its history puts the 1898 tower on shore just east of the pier; Rowlett puts it at the end of the breakwater on the east side of the harbour entrance. The story gives the entrance and Lighthouse Road position and names the disagreement.
LighthouseFriends and the City: restoration 2000 to 2002 (Friends of the Port Dalhousie Lighthouse); Rowlett: initial restoration 2002-03. The story states both.

notes_for_editor: NAMING: the record's 'Port Dalhousie Range Rear' is the Inner Range Light of the City of St. Catharines and the 'Rear Range (Lighthouse)' of the Register; LighthouseFriends calls it 'Port Dalhousie Range Rear'. The front (outer) range light of 1878/1879 is a separate structure and is not covered here. DISAGREEMENTS STATED IN THE STORY: (1) Location: LighthouseFriends map line (inner end of the east pier), LighthouseFriends history (on shore just east of the pier), Rowlett (end of the breakwater on the east side of the entrance). (2) Built: 1898 (City, LighthouseFriends, Register) against 1899 (Rowlett). (3) Restoration: 2000 to 2002 (City, LighthouseFriends) against 2002-03 (Rowlett). (4) Characteristic change: Department report 1 June 1901 against LighthouseFriends 1 June 1902. DISAGREEMENTS NOT USED IN THE STORY: Height: Rowlett 12 m (40 ft) against City 16 m (52 ft); the record's 12.0 m is kept and a human should check. Octagonal count (Register: one of four in the Great Lakes basin; City: one of three; LighthouseFriends: one of six) is not used. KEEPERS: David Hunter's line in the statement for the year ended 30 June 1902 (scan p. 235, printed p. 58) was checked on the page image: 'Hunter, David | Port Dalhousie | Oct. 29, 1879 | 350 00'. The other keepers come from LighthouseFriends' roster alone; their dates are LighthouseFriends' spans ('at least' where it says so). NOT FOUND: any wreck or rescue tied to this light in the sources read (the 1837 gale and 1898 fire are the only storm and fire events). A Chronicling America search for the August 1898 fire returned no pages. A fixed-red light is recorded for the year ended 30 June 1900. The keeper's daily work is described only in the City's note on the tower's sleeping quarters. No photos added.
